# Spec: verify-fix-loop
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-22 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-57 (report 19, A1) -->
<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->

## Overview

Today a FAIL from the verify stage blocks the entry `verdict`; `ledger.sh unblock` clears the block, the phase stays
`verify`, the verifier runs again on the same head, and the builder never sees the findings — a person carries
every round (16 rounds across HEF-22, HEF-25 and HEF-31). This feature makes a FAIL a **build-stage job**: the
launcher moves the entry from `verify` back to `implement` with a helper-generated *rework brief* (the failed gates'
evidence, as data, hashed — the merge-forward brief's pattern); the builder fixes the findings on the same branch,
pushes to the same PR, and hands back to verify — no person in between. `orchestrate.verify_rounds` (default 3)
caps the loop; past it, one `verdict` block whose open findings a person reads through `ledger.sh questions`. A
finding the builder disputes, or one whose fix would deviate from the spec, is a person's question, not a round.

## Context (as the code stands, cited)

- `hooks/session-launch.sh:395-422` — the verify transcription: every reported verdict is written with
  `ledger.sh verdict` (evidence ≤ 500 chars, schema `:558`); a missing required kind gate or review verdict is a FAIL;
  any FAIL → `ledger.sh block <id> --kind verdict` (`:420`), the phase stays `verify`. The transcription is shared by
  the headless run (`:755`, after `ledger.sh run` released the owner at `:746`) and the lane's `--finish` (`:459-460`).
- `commands/hef.orchestrate.md:163` — a `verdict` block's form: **Retry** → `ledger.sh unblock <id>` · **Later**.
  Retry re-runs the verifier on the unchanged head: the loop a person drives.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:536-572` — `advance` moves forward only. `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh:165-306` — `forward`, the
  mechanical backward move `pr → implement` with a generated, hashed brief (`<id>.forward-<n>.md`, `.forwards[]`),
  a cap of 3, and `--past-cap --by` as a person-only form (`hooks/lane-lib.sh:57`). This feature copies that shape.
- `hooks/session-launch-forward.sh` — the implement launch's merge-forward arm: `forward_open_row` (rows older than
  the last reopen are closed), `forward_prompt` (the brief and the person's answers as delimited data via
  `person_text_as_data`), `forward_schema` (the optional `question` field, only on that run, so
  `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt` stays byte-identical), `forward_transcribe_guard` (route kept, `pr_url` must be the
  row's), `implement_question_file` (the question beside the entry, `<!--` rewritten, ≤ 8000 bytes).
- `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh:109-120` — `questions_item` serves `human:clarify`, `human:plan-review`, and a `conflict`
  block that carries a `question_path`.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:294-298` — `launcher_gate`: `run`/`claim` only with `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1` and no session id.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:518-528` — implement claims count `attempts`; a third stalls the entry.
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:513-514` — the precedent for a validated round cap (`orchestrate.plan_review_rounds`,
  integer, refused otherwise, `false` refused).

## Decisions (made from the code; no open question needed)

- **D1 — a new move, `ledger.sh rework <id>`.** Called by the verify transcription in place of `block --kind verdict`
  when the run has at least one FAIL. It accepts phase `verify` only, unblocked, unowned, and moves the entry to
  `implement`, `owner = null`, `attempts = 0`, `blocked_on = null`, appending `.reworks[] = {n, pr_url, head_sha,
  sha256, at, by, consumed: false}` and an event `rework`. The plain form is **launcher-only** (`HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1`,
  no session id — `launcher_gate`'s rule): no session may bounce an entry between stages. `--past-cap --by <name>`
  is the person's form (D6).
- **D2 — the open findings are the latest verdict per gate that is `FAIL`, of the current verify round.** The move
  takes the entry's `.verdicts[]` written after its last implement run (`.runs[]`, role `implement`, its `at`; no
  such run → all), reduces them to the last verdict per gate (the same reduce the verified-head check applies to one
  run, `session-launch.sh:418`) and takes the FAILs — so an old FAIL of a gate this round omitted, or one from before a
  reopen, never reaches the brief. No FAIL among them → the move refuses (nothing to fix; constitution 5); inside the
  transcription that refusal becomes today's `verdict` block (FR-013b) — e.g. a run that reported a gate FAIL and then
  PASS ends blocked `verdict` for a person, as before this feature.
- **D3 — the brief is generated, not authored.** A fixed template: the item id, round n of the cap, the PR URL, the
  head SHA the verifier saw, and per open finding its gate, the verifier's session and its evidence; plus the
  verifier's run summary (≤ 2000 chars) when the launcher passes it (`--summary-file`). Written to
  `<ledger dir>/<id>.rework-<n>.md` (never through a link), sha256 in the row, re-hashed at launch, handed to the
  builder as delimited data. Every `<!--` in the evidence and summary is rewritten (`<!-\-`), as FR-012 of
  merge-forward does, so a comment strip cannot cut the brief short.
- **D4 — the builder fixes on the same branch and the same PR.** The rework prompt: re-run each failed gate's command
  first to see its full findings (the brief's evidence is capped at 500 chars per gate), fix the open findings, run the
  gate commands the findings name (the project's tests through `lane-build.sh` when the cache rule is printed),
  commit, `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` without force, outcome `pr` with the same `pr_url`. Never re-spec,
  re-plan, re-task, rebase, force-push or open a new PR. The launcher owns the ledger effects (merge-forward D15):
  the route is kept, an outcome `pr` naming another or no URL is transcribed `failed`, the row stays open.
- **D5 — disputes and spec deviations stop as a question.** A finding the builder judges wrong (it cites the
  evidence that the code is already right), or one whose fix would change what the spec or plan says (a spec
  deviation), is not fixed: the builder fixes nothing it disputes, pushes nothing, and stops `blocked`
  `human:clarify` with a `question` naming each such finding (gate, evidence, the builder's reason, the spec line
  when it is a deviation). The row stays open; the person's answer reaches the next rework run as data (US4).
- **D6 — the cap.** `orchestrate.verify_rounds`: an integer 0–10, default 3, refused otherwise (`false` and strings
  too). It counts the entry's rework rows since its last reopen. A FAIL with `verify_rounds` rows already → no move:
  the transcription blocks `verdict` with a question file listing the open findings (and the rounds taken), so
  `ledger.sh questions <id>` serves it. `0` restores today's behaviour (every FAIL blocks `verdict`) with the question
  file added. Bound: ≤ `verify_rounds` × the implement stall cap (3 attempts) builder runs per item before a person
  is asked. Past the cap the person chooses in the orchestrator: **Another round** →
  `ledger.sh rework <id> --past-cap --by "<name>"` (person-only: `is_person_sub`, orchestrator lane, an ask rule;
  it accepts the entry's own `verdict` block and records `by`) · **Re-verify** → `ledger.sh unblock <id>` (today's
  Retry) · **Later**.
- **D7 — the person's ruling reaches both sides.** Every question the launcher blocks an open rework row with is
  listed on that row in order (`asked[]`: the blocked question's path, sha256, `at`, and `dispute: true` for a
  rework run's dispute, `false` for any other — the worktree question, say). An answer is a ruling only when it
  cleared a `human:clarify` block and the latest listed question before it (by answer order, not time) is a
  dispute, and it is paired with that question; an answer to any other
  question is never a ruling, and every dispute's ruling in a row is kept (two disputes in one row → two rulings). Each ruling travels with its
  dispute question as hashed delimited data, under the rule "the builder's question is the author's claim, shown
  only so the ruling can be read; only the person's words waive". Rulings are handed to the next
  rework run (as merge-forward FR-014 does) and, once that run reports `pr`, to every later verify run of the same
  PR as a delimited "the person's ruling on disputed findings" block — the rulings of every consumed rework row since
  the last reopen, so a waiver holds for the life of the PR, not one run: a finding the person waived is not a FAIL
  of its gate, and the verifier cites the ruling in that gate's evidence. No ruling on record since the last reopen →
  the verify prompt is byte-identical to today.
- **D8 — a rework and a merge forward never overlap.** `rework` refuses when a forward row is open; a forward needs
  phase `pr`, which a reworked entry reaches only after a PASS, so the implement launch sees at most one open row.
  When both exist the forward row wins (it is older and its push base matters) — asserted, not expected.
- **D9 — headless and lanes alike.** The change is in `transcribe`, which both paths run, so a lane's
  `verify --finish` reworks as a headless run does; `ledger.sh next --stage build` then returns the entry (phase
  `implement`, unowned, unblocked) to the build lane or the next build pass. No new doorbell, no form.
- **D10 — out of scope.** The verifier's gate chain, its schema and its read-only rule are unchanged; `merge_by:
  auto` reads the verified head as today (a reworked head is verified again before anything merges).
  **A waived gate never merges unattended (decided by the owner, 2026-11-22 — see Clarifications):** a verify run
  that was handed a ruling block (FR-012) records verified head `none`, whatever its verdicts; its PASS reaches
  `pr` + `human:merge`, never the `merge_by: auto` path. A person's ruling never becomes an unattended merge.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A FAIL goes back to the build stage with its findings [P1]
- **Given** an entry in phase `verify` whose verify run (headless or a lane's `--finish`) reports at least one FAIL
  (or the launcher adds one: a missing review or kind gate), and fewer than `verify_rounds` rework rows since its
  last reopen
- **When** the launcher transcribes the run
- **Then** it writes the verdicts as today, then runs `ledger.sh rework <id> --summary-file <f>`: the entry moves to
  `implement`, unowned, unblocked, `attempts = 0`, with an open rework row and a hashed brief listing every open
  finding; `ledger.sh next --stage build` returns it; no form is shown, no `verdict` block written.
- **Edge:** a FAIL and a later PASS for the same gate in one run → that gate is not an open finding (latest wins);
  if it was the only FAIL, `rework` refuses "nothing to fix" and the launcher writes today's `verdict` block (FR-013b).
- **Edge:** `verify_rounds` 0 → no move; `verdict` block with the findings question (US3).
- **Error:** `rework` on an entry not in `verify`, blocked, owned, terminal, with no FAIL among the latest verdicts,
  with an open forward row, or called without the launcher marker (and without `--past-cap`) → non-zero exit naming
  what it saw, entry byte-identical (constitution 5).
- **Must NOT:** write a `verdict` block below the cap; leave the entry in `verify`; call `ledger.sh directive`.
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch.sh` (verify transcription), a new sourced `hooks/session-launch-rework.sh`,
  `hooks/ledger.sh` (dispatch, usage), `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh` or a new `hooks/ledger-rework.sh`,
  `hooks/lane-lib.sh`; tests: a new `tests/smoke-rework.sh`.

### US2: The builder fixes and hands back to verify [P1]
- **Given** an `implement` entry with an open rework row
- **When** the implement launch runs (headless, or a lane's `--prepare`)
- **Then** the brief's hash is checked (mismatch → die, nothing launched), the prompt carries the brief as data and
  the rework instruction (D4); on outcome `pr` with the same URL the row is marked consumed and the entry advances to
  `verify`; the verifier runs its full chain on the new head; a PASS reaches `pr` + `human:merge` (or the auto path)
  as today; a FAIL starts round n+1.
- **Edge:** the worker reports `failed` → the row stays open, the implement stall cap applies as today.
- **Error:** outcome `pr` with another or no `pr_url` → transcribed `failed`, the URL not recorded, the row open.
- **Must NOT** (instruction-level, in the rework rule; the launcher trusts outcome `pr` as it does for every
  implement run today, and `merge_by: auto` merges only the PR head it verified): re-spec, re-plan, re-task, rebase,
  force-push, open a new PR, or report `pr` with a fix left unpushed.
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch.sh` (implement prompt selection, transcription), `hooks/session-launch-rework.sh`.

### US3: The cap blocks once, with the open findings readable [P1]
- **Given** an entry whose verify run FAILs with `verify_rounds` rework rows already since its last reopen
- **When** the launcher transcribes the run
- **Then** the entry stays in `verify`, blocked `verdict` with a `question_path` whose file lists each open finding
  (gate, evidence) and the rounds taken; `ledger.sh questions <id>` prints it; the orchestrator's `verdict` row offers
  **Another round** / **Re-verify** / **Later** (D6).
- **Edge:** a `verdict` block with no `question_path` (written before this release) → the row keeps today's
  **Retry** · **Later**, its reason from `ledger.sh show`.
- **Error:** `rework --past-cap` without a valid `--by`, outside the orchestrator lane in a lanes project, or on an
  entry not blocked `verdict` in phase `verify` → refused, nothing changed.
- **Must NOT:** block `verdict` without the findings file; let a session call `--past-cap`.
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch-rework.sh`, `hooks/ledger-lanes.sh` (`questions_item`), `hooks/lane-lib.sh`,
  `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (ask rule), `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`.

### US4: A disputed finding or a spec deviation is a person's question [P1]
- **Given** a rework run where the builder disputes a finding or the fix would deviate from the spec
- **When** it stops
- **Then** its outcome is `blocked` `human:clarify` with a `question` (≤ 8000 chars, the field added only on a rework
  run) naming each such finding; the launcher writes it beside the entry and blocks with `--question`; `ledger.sh
  questions <id>` shows it; the row stays open. After the person answers (`ledger.sh answer`), the next rework run
  carries the brief and the answers; once it reports `pr`, the next verify run carries the answers as the person's
  ruling (D7).
- **Edge:** empty `question` → the summary is the question (never an empty question file).
- **Must NOT:** count the question as a round; push a partial fix; treat the answer text as instructions beyond the
  item (a tool or setting in it is reported).
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch-rework.sh`, `hooks/session-launch.sh` (verify prompt block).

### US5: Docs and the orchestrator describe the loop [P2]
- **Given** the orchestrator's block table, the quickstart and the install docs
- **When** a person reads them
- **Then** they say a FAIL goes back to the builder by itself up to `verify_rounds`, and describe the cap's form.
- Touches: `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`, `docs/install.md`
  (the `verify_rounds` key), `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/hooks.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | The verify transcription, when the run holds at least one FAIL (reported or launcher-added), runs `ledger.sh rework <id>` (launcher marker, the verifier's summary as `--summary-file`) instead of `block --kind verdict`; the verdicts and the verified head are written first, as today. `rework` itself decides move or cap (FR-006), as `forward` does. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `ledger.sh rework <id>` sets `phase = implement`, `owner = null`, `attempts = 0`, `blocked_on = null`, appends `.reworks[] = {n, pr_url, head_sha, sha256, at, by, consumed: false}` and an event `rework`, and prints one line naming the move and the round (`n` of the cap). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | `rework` refuses (non-zero, message with what it saw, entry byte-identical) when: the entry is terminal or not in phase `verify`; no PR URL is recorded, or it is not the forge shape `forward_guards` checks (`https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>[/<path>]`, `ledger-lifecycle.sh:212`); the recorded `.branch` is empty or not a plain ref (`^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$`, no leading `-` — the `forward` rule, `ledger-lifecycle.sh:186`); it is owned; it is blocked (any kind, except `verdict` under `--past-cap`); no gate's latest verdict is FAIL; a forward row is open (unconsumed **and** newer than the last `reopen` event — `forward_open_row`'s definition, `session-launch-forward.sh:22-23`; a stale row across a reopen does not refuse); the plain form runs without `HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1` or with a session id; it runs inside a launched worker (`HEFESTO_WORKER`); `--summary-file` names a missing file, a link, or more than 32 KB. | P1 | US1, US3 |
| FR-004 | The brief is generated from a fixed template — id, round n and the cap, PR URL, the head SHA the verifier saw, per open finding (latest verdict per gate = FAIL) its gate, `by` and evidence, then the summary when given — with every `<!--` rewritten to `<!-\-`, written to `<ledger dir>/<id>.rework-<n>.md` (any existing file there removed first, never written through a link), its sha256 in the row. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | `orchestrate.verify_rounds` is read and validated by `rework`, and by the verify launch before anything is launched (the same rule in both; `session-launch.sh` does not source `lane-lib.sh`, so each carries the one jq expression and the smoke test runs both against the same bad values): an integer 0–10, absent → 3; any other value (a string, `false`, a fraction, out of range) dies naming the value and the expected shape. | P1 | US1, US3 |
| FR-006 | At the cap (rows since the last reopen ≥ `verify_rounds`; without `--past-cap`), `rework` — after every FR-003 refusal — writes `<ledger dir>/<id>.question-<ts>.md` listing each open finding (gate, evidence) and the rounds taken (`<!--` rewritten, ≤ 8000 bytes), and blocks `verdict` with `--question`; `questions_item` admits a `verdict` block that carries a `question_path`. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-007 | `rework --past-cap --by <name>` is person-only (`is_person_sub` in `hooks/lane-lib.sh`, so lane-guard and `ledger.sh` admit it from the orchestrator lane only; an ask rule in `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` in both spellings and in its `--check` array); it accepts an entry in `verify` blocked `verdict`, skips the count, keeps every other FR-003 refusal, records `by` in the row and the event. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-008 | The implement launch, for an entry with an open rework row (and no open forward row — D8), verifies the brief's sha256 (mismatch or a missing file → die, nothing launched) and builds the rework prompt: the brief as delimited data, the person's unconsumed answers as delimited data, each ruling's dispute question beside its answer (D7; paired by the same rule `--rework-consumed` stamps with), and the instruction of D4 and D5. The prompt names the PR URL, the branch, and the protected branches. The branch is the one the launch's worktree `<repo top>/.claude/worktrees/<id>` is on (read as `record_worktree` reads it), checked as a plain ref and equal to the entry's `.branch`; a worktree that is missing, not a worktree, or on another branch → a question file naming the path and both branches, `block --kind human:clarify --question`, nothing launched (the `forward_wt_check` shape — never `claude -w` on a fresh branch), recorded on the open row with `record --rework-asked other` (FR-010) so its answer is never a ruling. | P1 | US2, US4 |
| FR-009 | On a rework run the implement schema gains the optional `question` string (≤ 8000); every other implement launch keeps the 9.2.0 schema and prompt, so `tests/fixtures/launch-920.txt` stays byte-identical. | P1 | US4 |
| FR-010 | On a rework run's transcription: the entry's route is kept (the reported one is not recorded); outcome `pr` whose `pr_url` differs from the row's (or is empty) is transcribed `failed` without recording that URL; on a matching `pr` the row is marked consumed (`ledger.sh record <id> --rework-consumed`, which in one jq step stamps the row's `ruling` with the unconsumed answers' indices, then marks the row and those answers consumed — no flag-order dependency) before `advance verify`; on `blocked human:clarify` the question (or, empty, the summary) goes to a question file (`<!--` rewritten, ≤ 8000 bytes) passed as `block --question`, then `ledger.sh record <id> --rework-asked dispute` appends to the open row's `asked[]` the path and sha256 of the question the entry's block carries (`blocked_on.question_path` — never a caller-chosen file) its `at`, `dispute: true`, and `answers_before` (`.answers | length` at record time) (D7); the FR-008 worktree question is recorded the same way with `--rework-asked other` (`dispute: false`); `--rework-consumed` stamps as `ruling` each unconsumed answer at index i whose `kind` is `human:clarify` and whose last `asked[]` entry with `answers_before == i` is a dispute (the block that answer cleared; a block with no recorded entry leaves its answer unpaired), paired with that entry (ordinal, never by timestamp — `at` has 1-second resolution; an answer to a `human:plan-review` block is never a ruling), each stamped entry self-describing (the answer's and the dispute question's path and sha256); on `blocked` or `failed` the row stays open. Both `record` flags are launcher-only (`HEFESTO_LAUNCHER=1`, no session id, not inside a worker — the `--verified-head` gate, `ledger-automerge.sh:44-49`); anything else is refused, entry unchanged. | P1 | US2, US4 |
| FR-011 | The rework instruction requires, for a disputed finding or a fix that would change what the spec or plan states: no fix of it, no push, outcome `blocked`, `blocked_on: human:clarify`, and a `question` listing per such finding its gate, evidence, the builder's reason, and the spec/plan line for a deviation. A finding the person's answer waives is left alone; when every open finding is waived or fixed by the answer's terms and nothing is left to change, the builder reports outcome `pr` with the same `pr_url` and no new commit (the waiver path), so the ruling reaches the verifier (FR-012). | P1 | US4 |
| FR-012 | The verify launch, when any consumed rework row dated after the entry's last `reopen` event carries a ruling (answers recorded while that row was open, indexed on it at consumption), adds one delimited "person's ruling" block holding all of them (hashed like every person text; mismatch → die) telling the verifier a waived finding is not a FAIL and to cite the ruling in that gate's evidence; with no such answer the verify prompt and schema are byte-identical to today. A verify run that was handed the ruling block records verified head `none` (D10, the owner's decision): the transcription derives "ruled" from the entry by the same jq expression the prompt used (unchanged between `--prepare` and `--finish`, the entry being owned), so its PASS reaches `pr` + `human:merge` even under `merge_by: auto`. "Handed a ruling" is the mechanical stand-in for "passed only because of a waiver" — conservative by design. | P2 | US4 |
| FR-013 | A rework row older than the entry's last `reopen` event is closed (not open, not counted, no ruling), as `forward_open_row` treats forward rows; `rework` marks every earlier row consumed before it appends the new one, and the rework prompt hashes and hands in the open row's brief only — never every unconsumed row. | P1 | US1, US3 |
| FR-013a | `rework`, on the move, also sets `attempts = 0` (each round gets the implement stall cap afresh) and marks every earlier answer consumed (an answer to a plan question never steers a fix); `--head` takes a full 40- or 64-hex sha or nothing (→ `null`), any other value refused before a write; the row's `head_sha` and the `rework` event carry it. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-013b | When `rework` exits non-zero inside the verify transcription, the launcher prints the refusal on stderr and falls back to today's `block --kind verdict`, so the entry is never left in `verify` unblocked and unowned (verify claims count no attempts — a relaunch loop); when that fallback fails too, the launcher exits non-zero, as today's line does. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-014 | The orchestrator's `verdict` row: with a `question_path`, it shows `ledger.sh questions <id>` and offers **Another round** → `ledger.sh rework <id> --past-cap --by "<name>"` · **Re-verify** → `ledger.sh unblock <id>` · **Later**; without one, today's **Retry** · **Later**. | P2 | US3, US5 |
| FR-015 | Docs (`hef.orchestrate.md`, quickstart EN + pt-BR, `install.md` with the `verify_rounds` key, `architecture.md`, `docs/hooks.md` — the `ledger.sh` row gains `rework`, a row for each new sourced file: `ledger-rework.sh`, `session-launch-rework.sh`, `rework-pairs.sh`) and a `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry describe the loop; `rework` is listed in `ledger.sh` usage. | P2 | US5 |
| FR-016 | Every new guard has a mutation check in `tests/smoke-rework.sh` or `tests/smoke-rework-ruling.sh` (the move and the ruling, split so each stays under 500 code lines; reintroduce the defect, the suite goes red): the FAIL → rework routing; below-cap vs at-cap; `verify_rounds` 0 and its validation; each FR-003 refusal (phase, owner, block, no FAIL, open forward, launcher marker, worker, summary file); latest-verdict-per-gate; the brief hash check; the `<!--` rewrite; the reopen cutoff; the route keep and `pr_url` check; consumed only on `pr`; the `question` field only on a rework run; `--past-cap`'s person-only gate and its `verdict`-block admission; `questions_item` admitting `verdict`; the verify ruling block present only with a ruling, its reopen cutoff, and its persistence across a later round; the earlier rows consumed on a move and the open-row-only brief (a stale row across a reopen); the `attempts` reset; the answers consumed on a move; the `--head` validation; the refusal fallback to `block verdict`; the lane paths (a verify `--finish` FAIL that reworks; an implement `--prepare`/`--finish` rework run with the `question` schema and the row consumed); `rework` launcher-only in `tests/smoke-signatures.sh` (no allow rule, adding it to `LEDGER_ALLOW` goes red); the PR-URL and branch-shape refusals; the rework worktree check; the waiver sentence in the rework prompt; the current-round filter of D2 (an older FAIL of an omitted gate is not in the brief); `hefesto-setup.sh --check` failing without the `rework --past-cap` ask rule; `rework <id> --summary-file f --past-cap` without `--by` refused (the parser, not only `is_launcher_sub`); `--rework-consumed` stamping the ruling on its own; a non-dispute answer (e.g. to the worktree question) kept out of the ruling block; a stale forward row across a reopen not refusing `rework`; the round number printed as the count since the last reopen; a verify run handed a ruling block that reports all PASS records verified head `none` and ends blocked `human:merge` under `merge_by: auto` (dropping the `none` override makes it advance unblocked — red), in headless and lane `--finish` alike; `record --rework-consumed` and `record --rework-asked` each refused from a session and from a worker (removing the gate goes red); two disputes in one row → both rulings reach the verify prompt; a worktree question asked after a dispute → its answer is not a ruling; `lane-guard.sh` denies plain `ledger.sh rework <id>` in every lane, admits `rework <id> --past-cap --by x` in the orchestrator lane and denies it in a stage lane (mutation: `:166` reverted to `is_launcher_sub "$SUB"`); `rework_route` returning non-zero when both `rework` and the fallback `block --kind verdict` fail; an answer to a `human:plan-review` block after a dispute is not a ruling; the rework prompt and `--rework-consumed` pair answers identically; a changed dispute-question or answer file behind a stamped ruling kills the verify launch; removing `session-launch-rework.sh` or `rework-pairs.sh` makes its loader die with a hefesto message (the `ledger-rework.sh` removal case joins `tests/smoke-lifecycle.sh:159,164`). | P1 | all |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | A fixture entry in `verify` goes, with a fake verifier reporting `review: FAIL`, to `implement` with an open rework row and no block; with a fake builder reporting `pr` on the same URL, back to `verify`, the row consumed; with a fake verifier reporting all PASS, to `pr` blocked `human:merge` — every step a launcher call, no `ledger.sh` command a person would run (no `unblock`, `answer`, `record --reviewed-by-human`). | `tests/smoke-rework.sh` |
| SC-002 | With `verify_rounds: 2`, the third FAIL leaves the entry in `verify` blocked `verdict`, and `ledger.sh questions <id>` prints every open finding's gate and evidence; `rework --past-cap --by p` then moves it (outside a lane) and is refused from a non-orchestrator lane. | `tests/smoke-rework.sh` |
| SC-003 | A fake builder reporting `blocked human:clarify` with a dispute `question` ends blocked `human:clarify`, `ledger.sh questions` prints the dispute, the row still open, the round count unchanged; after `ledger.sh answer`, the next implement prompt carries the brief and the answer, and after its `pr` the next verify prompt carries the ruling block. | `tests/smoke-rework-ruling.sh` |
| SC-004 | Each FR-016 mutation, applied in-test with `sed` to a scratch copy, makes its assertion fail (`bad "mutation survived: …"`). | `tests/smoke-rework.sh`, `tests/smoke-rework-ruling.sh` |

## Clarifications
_No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker: every point was decided from the code and the item's text (D1–D10). The board item
fixes the default cap (3), the config key, the data-and-hash brief, and that disputes and spec deviations go to a
person; the merge-forward precedent (HEF-31) fixes the shape of the move, the brief, the cap's person-only override,
and the launcher's ownership of the run's ledger effects._

### Session 2026-11-22 (the owner's answer to plan review round 3, change 2)
- Q: May a verify run that passes a gate only because a person waived a finding record a verified head, so
  `merge_by: auto` can merge it? → A: **No.** When a verify run passes a gate only because a person waived a
  finding, it records no verified head (`none`). A waived gate always reaches `human:merge`; a ruling never becomes
  an unattended merge under `merge_by: auto`. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-22. (Applied in D10, FR-012, FR-016.)

### Session 2026-11-22 (the owner's answer after plan review reached its cap)
- Q: Plan review reached the cap (5) with every requested revision applied — approve the plan as it stands? → A:
  **Approved.** The owner approves the plan as it stands (commit 142e9c5, including the two round-5 fixes made after
  the cap) on 2026-11-22; tasks.md is written from it, with no further plan-review rounds.
